synopsis: Operator-already-reacting detection avoids adding automatic braking when the operator is already stopping or steering safely away; unnecessary braking can jolt a loaded machine and shift its load [f13960, f13961]. ISO 21815-3:2023 forbids overriding stronger operator braking, while UN R131 and R152 allow conscious driver actions to interrupt automatic braking; these override provisions do not establish validated off-road reaction-detection logic [f5913, f5943, f13971]. The recommended production approach fuses operator commands with machine response, crediting sufficient achieved deceleration or a demonstrably safer evasive trajectory rather than control movement alone [f13967, f13968, f6336, f6342]. Throttle release is particularly weak evidence because a downhill machine can still accelerate, and standing down after a startled operator briefly touches a control can collapse the stopping margin [f13970, f13969]. No off-road validation was found, so the program should define the reaction state machine before hardware arrives and test it in operator-in-the-loop and physical trials [f6332, f13972]. The architecture guidance is not fully aligned: Chapter 8 calls suppression a secondary layer at a_measured ≥ a_required, whereas the glossary calls it a third layer and recommends an additional deceleration margin [f6402, f13884, f13968].
